scope.summary: No product change was needed: the terminal-effect fix already ships (a succeeded held execute/checkpoint/undo is recognized as terminal so a late-deadline expiry never reports RETRYABLE for done work — DI1 2e54c6a9, DI6 124d62c1). What was missing and is added here is the end-to-end regression guard: three tests drive the SAME async boundary the server uses (ToolDispatch::dispatch, where cx.is_cancel_requested() && !terminal_result decides Cancelled vs Ok) through the naive client retry loop, inducing the finalization-window race and proving the effect is applied exactly once.
out_of_scope: the terminal-effect production logic itself (already correct; DI1 2e54c6a9 / DI6 124d62c1, unchanged here)

entry_points.name: held-effect exactly-once regression at the deadline boundary
entry_points.trace: crates/oraclemcp/src/dispatch/tests.rs: three tests induce the finalization-window race (cancel_on_execute trips the cancel bit AFTER the wire effect returns) through ToolDispatch::dispatch and prove no held-effect double-apply. Regression guard landed in 0aceec11 and was rustfmt-only touched at source 5031d67e; the exactly-once product behavior it guards is 2e54c6a9 / 124d62c1. Mutation-verified per the landing commit. cargo test -p oraclemcp dispatch.

limitations: This close adds a regression guard for behavior that was already correct in production; no dispatch product code changed. Scoped test proof; full gate green in CI at HEAD 5031d67e. source.sha is the last commit touching dispatch/tests.rs (5031d67e, rustfmt after the tests landed in 0aceec11).
